description: Partial-word replacement: the LEADING and TRAILING phrases of the REPLACING phrase of COPY (ISO §2023:7.2.3.2) and of the REPLACE statement format 1 (ISO §2023:7.2.4.2) - `LEADING | TRAILING ==partial-word-1== BY ==partial-word-2==`, matched against the leftmost / rightmost characters of ONE text-word (§2023:7.2.3.4 GR9b, §2023:7.2.4.4 GR8b). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 COPY REPLACING replaces 'each properly matched occurrence of pseudo-text-1, identifier-1, word-1, and literal-1 in the library text' (§1985:XII.2.4 GR3) and the 1985 REPLACE is REPLACE { ==pseudo-text-1== BY ==pseudo-text-2== } ... (§1985:XII.3.2; §1985:XII.3.4 GR1: 'Each matched occurrence of pseudo-text-1 in the source program is replaced by the corresponding pseudo-text-2'), with no partial-word operand; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 adds LEADING / TRAILING ==partial-word-1== BY ==partial-word-2== to both general formats (§2002:7.1.2.1, §2002:7.1.3.1; §2002:7.1.2.3 GR10b and §2002:7.1.3.3 GR8b: 'When the LEADING phrase is specified, partial-word-1 matches ...') and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 41: 'COPY and REPLACE statement partial word replacement. LEADING and TRAILING phrases of the REPLACE statement and the REPLACING phrase of the COPY statement allow replacement of partial words in source text and library text.' 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.2.2.3 GR10b). VCR row 7.33; the sibling ALSO / LAST row replace-also-last-2002 has the same 2002 edge. ONE gate, asked by the one parser of both statements' operands (CopyProcessor.ParseReplacingOperands through OperandScreen.PartialWord, once per statement; kb/Work PB1670).
display: the LEADING / TRAILING partial-word phrases of COPY REPLACING and REPLACE
vcr: §2002:7.1.2.1 / §2002:7.1.3.1 partial-word phrases; the edge quoted from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965); VCR row 7.33
